title: Karger step factors bound the survival-probability product
statement:
Let $T$ be a surviving trace of $\mathrm{steps}$ steps, with states $s_0, s_1, \dots$; write $G_i$ for the multigraph and $C_i$ for the distinguished cut in state $s_i$, and let $n_i$ and $m_i$ denote the vertex count and edge count of $G_i$. Suppose the initial cut $C_0$ is a minimum cut of $G_0$, and that $n_i \ge 2$ for every index $i < \mathrm{steps}$. Then, writing $c$ for the size of $C_0$,
\[
  \prod_{i < \mathrm{steps}} \frac{n_i - 2}{n_i}
  \;\le\;
  \prod_{i < \mathrm{steps}} \left(1 - \frac{c}{m_i}\right),
\]
the right-hand factors being the one-step survival probabilities for cut size $c$ and edge count $m_i$.
hypotheses_covered: T is a surviving trace of length steps
the initial cut C_0 is a minimum cut of G_0
for every index i < steps, the graph G_i has at least two vertices (n_i ≥ 2)
c is the size of the initial cut C_0
replaced:
If the initial cut is a min-cut and every graph along the first $\text{steps}$ indices has
at least two vertices, then
\[
  \prod_{i<\text{steps}} \frac{n_i-2}{n_i} \;\le\;
  \prod_{i<\text{steps}} \mathrm{survivalProb}\bigl(\,\text{initial cut size},\;
  \text{edge count at }i\,\bigr),
\]
where $n_i$ is the vertex count at index $i$.
